pos.personaBrief: Cruzeiro had superior possession (Lance, Fluminense 5-2) and Alex says the team sought the ball and never defended deep; the team played with the ball, not on the counter.

pro.personaBrief: Alex describes tabelamos, driblamos, buscamos espaço, with Maldonado excellent at passing; build-up was short and combinative with quick transitions (Lance retrospective).

est.personaBrief: Alex, Mota and Wendel moved between the lines and the team was built around Alex; combinations in short spaces, with a roaming striker and 10 rather than rigid zones.

lar.personaBrief: Width is unverified: general knowledge says the 2003 side used a central 4-4-2 or diamond with Alex and no true wingers, attacking through the middle and with full-backs.

blo.personaBrief: Lance retrospective cites high pressing and quick transitions, and Alex says the team never played deep; pressing mechanics themselves are thinly documented.

mar.personaBrief: No source on marking; Maldonado is described as positioning to intercept passing lines, and Brazilian teams of 2003 mostly used zonal marking, so this is general knowledge.

pla.personaBrief: The team kept its attacking identity everywhere (Alex: never defended in any stadium), and Luxemburgo shaped the side around Alex, though he trained for the final and punished a game where they disrespected the opponent.

res.personaBrief: An attacking, possession team that never retreated, with a record-setting 102 goals, but whose aim was winning the Triple Crown; Luxemburgo is a winner but his side did not park the bus.

sis.personaBrief: Luxemburgo built the team around Alex and backed him against the president, but demanded the whole group do its job; the quality of the stars (Alex, Aristizabal, Cris, Maldonado) was the base.

jog.personaBrief: Technical team: Alex the classic captain 10 with short dribbles and vertical passes, Maldonado valued for passing excellence and clean tackling.

bas.personaBrief: A squad of veterans and free signings (Alex, Aristizabal at 32, Zinho 36, Maldonado); Felipe Melo was a boy and a substitute; Alex said the references were the veterans.

lid.personaBrief: Luxemburgo is a strong, authoritative boss who said he is the coach and took responsibility for the Alex bet; he handled reserve veterans like Zinho, with firm control of the group.
